comparison: RQ2 (Section VI-B), Tables III-V and VII-VIII: with context supplementation ('C') vs. without ('N'), within each model x knowledge (Nk/Ok/Sk) x prompt-scheme cell
model_config: Same model within each cell (GPT-4.1, Phi-3-mini-128k, Llama-3-8B, o4-mini, DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B); provider-default config, temperature 0 (o4-mini excepted); identical knowledge prefix and prompt scheme in both arms
dataset_metric: UniVul (Solidity, Java, C/C++; 147 vulnerable + 147 non-vulnerable); TP counts, precision, recall, F1 as annotated by GPT-4.1
budget_control: not controlled / not reported; the C arm appends extra code (callees, plus report-mentioned related functions for vulnerable samples) to the same prompt, so it is longer
arm_a: Target code + knowledge prefix + prompt scheme, plus static-analysis-extracted context: callees for all samples and related functions mentioned in the vulnerability report for vulnerable samples
arm_b: Target code + the same knowledge prefix and prompt scheme, no supplementary context
other_changes: none in the pipeline (context is 'processed before feeding the code into LLMs' via static analysis). Caveat: the report-derived related-function context exists only for vulnerable samples, so the added context is label-correlated
delta: "For Solidity, 22 out of 36 model–prompt–knowledge combinations show an increase in TPs with context, while 11 show a decrease. In Java, 18 combinations show an increase and 15 a decrease. C/C++ ... 28 combinations showing increased TPs and only 7 showing a decrease." (counts of cells, not pp)
rationale: Same model and prompt; only the supplied context differs ('we use static analysis to ensure the same contexts for the given code across all models'), but the context arm adds code and no length/token control is reported, so representation is confounded with context amount. The prior's 'same model/budget' claim is unsupported; additionally, report-mentioned related code is added only for vulnerable samples.

comparison: Table 4 (RQ3, Section 5.3): Multi-round SIFT (MSIVD-) vs. Multi-round SIFT + GNN (MSIVD) on BigVul
model_config: Both arms start from the same multitask-fine-tuned CodeLlama-13B-Instruct, but the classifier differs: MSIVD- converts it to sequence classification 'using a single linear layer'; MSIVD trains a separate sequence-to-classification model (DeepDFA GGNN adapter, embeddings concatenated with LLM hidden states, model dim 4352, 11 layers, LR 1e-6, 5 epochs; Table 2). Training configuration of the MSIVD- head is not separately reported
budget_control: not applicable as a prompt budget; same 2048-token context window in both arms. Trainable parameters and training procedure differ
arm_a: Fine-tuned LLM hidden states concatenated with GGNN embeddings learned over CFG-based dataflow (DFA) features
arm_b: Fine-tuned LLM hidden states with a single linear classification layer
other_changes: Architecture (added GNN adapter layers, larger model dimension), and a separate classification training loop with its own hyperparameters; the graph is not an input to the LLM but a jointly trained neural module
delta: "the additional GNN (multi-round SIFT + GNN) provides an additional 0.02 F1 on top of multi-round SIFT for the BigVul dataset" (F1 0.90 -> 0.92, absolute)
rationale: MSIVD- 'converts the first model into a sequence-to-classification model directly, using a single linear layer', whereas MSIVD adds GNN layers trained in a separate loop (Table 2: model dim 4352, 11 layers, LR 1e-6), so model architecture and training differ between arms, not just the representation supplied. No same-model input-only comparison exists in the paper.

comparison: Table III (Section III-C): RAG + CoT vs. No RAG
model_config: GPT-4o in both arms with the CoT prompt; other configuration (temperature etc.) not reported
dataset_metric: Big-Vul balanced test set (5,000 instances, 1:1); accuracy, precision, recall, F1
budget_control: not reported; the RAG arm adds a retrieved CWE/CVE record to the prompt, so it is longer
arm_a: Code snippet + CoT prompt + one retrieved Big-Vul record (top-5 by OpenAI embedding similarity from a 500-instance ChromaDB store, then 'GPT-4o later examines these records and selects the best one')
arm_b: Code snippet + CoT prompt, no retrieval
other_changes: Retrieval stage removed: embedding lookup in a vector DB plus an extra GPT-4o selection step over the top-5 candidates
delta: F1 33.49% (RAG + CoT) vs 23.92% (No RAG), i.e. 9.57 pp; accuracy 89.68% vs 76.42%
rationale: The ablation removes 'the RAG component', which is a pipeline stage (vector DB retrieval plus a GPT-4o step that 'examines these records and selects the best one') that also changes what is shown. The added-context arm is longer, with no budget control. It is not a representation-only swap.

comparison: Table 4 (Section 5.1): DeepSeek-R1 + CoT at API Level 3 (A3) vs. without API Level (w/o)
model_config: DeepSeek-R1 with Chain-of-Thought prompt in both arms; temperature 0.1, max_tokens 512 (output)
dataset_metric: NVD-derived C dataset (623 CVE samples); F1 (also accuracy/precision/recall)
budget_control: not controlled; the API abstraction is 'directly appending them to the corresponding target functions', so A3 is longer than w/o. max_tokens=512 caps output only
arm_a: Target function + appended Primitive API summary (concrete branches of primitive APIs + number of calls, from control-/call-graph analysis of callees)
other_changes: none (same model, same prompt strategy, abstraction produced offline by static analysis)
rationale: Model and CoT prompt are fixed and only the appended API context differs, but 'we incorporate the information from different API levels as supplementary ... details, directly appending them to the corresponding target functions' with no input-length control, so the structured arm is strictly longer. A1-A4 comparisons are cleaner against each other but are not reported as length-matched either.

comparison: Section 5.7 (RQ3), Figure 10: full LTFix vs. LTFix-NT (no context trace)
model_config: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, same role-play + structured CoT prompting in both arms; 5 runs, result valid if consistent in at least 4/5
dataset_metric: Custom benchmark of 49 memory errors from 14 C projects; number of correct patches, total errors fixed, new errors introduced
budget_control: not controlled between arms; the full arm adds the typestate-guided context trace to the prompt. The reported token analysis compares LTFix with the complete (unfiltered) context trace and SWE-agent, not with LTFix-NT
arm_a: Error report + error-propagation path + typestate-guided context trace (memory-state snapshots at typestate-changing operations)
arm_b: Error report + error-propagation path, context trace omitted
other_changes: none ('LTFix-NT omits the context trace in the prompts while maintaining all other components unchanged')
delta: "22 correct patches, demonstrating a 47% improvement over LTFix-NT" (22 vs 15, relative); total errors fixed 37 vs 22 ("68% improvement", relative); new errors introduced 1 (LTFix) vs 4 (LTFix-NT)
rationale: Same LLM and prompt, and only the context trace is removed ('omits the context trace in the prompts while maintaining all other components unchanged'), but the full arm is strictly longer and no per-arm token budget is reported. LTFix-F and LTFix-M change the context content more broadly (files or backtrace methods instead of path and trace), with no length reported.

comparison: Section V-B / Figure 3: retrieval-augmented k-shot vs. random k-shot prompting at the same k (10-shot reported in text). The record's cited comparison (Table I, 20-shot retrieval vs zero-shot) was also checked
model_config: Gemini-1.5-Flash in all prompting arms; 'a consistent prompt template across all few-shot experiments, regardless of how the in-context examples are selected'; decoding settings not reported
dataset_metric: Draper VDISC-derived snippets (Russell et al. 2018), CWE-119/120/469/476, multi-label; micro F1 (also subset, Hamming and partial-match accuracy)
budget_control: Example count matched (k examples in both arms); token length per prompt not reported. For the cited zero-shot vs 20-shot comparison, the retrieval arm adds 20 examples to an example-free prompt, so it is not controlled
arm_a: Task description + k in-context examples (code + labels) selected by gemini-embedding-001 cosine similarity from ChromaDB + test code
arm_b: Task description + k randomly sampled in-context examples (code + labels) + test code
other_changes: none beyond the example-selection mechanism (both arms show k labelled examples from the same training pool)
delta: 10-shot F1 71.43% (retrieval-augmented) vs 65.69% (random), +5.74 pp (Section V-B). The cited figure: 74.05% (20-shot retrieval) vs 36.35% (zero-shot), +37.70 pp, but that pair differs in context amount
rationale: Random vs retrieval-augmented prompting at equal k uses the same model and template and differs only in which examples are shown ('Random Prompting follows at 65.69%' vs 71.43% at 10 shots), so it is the clean comparison. The record's cited zero-shot vs 20-shot pair is only R-unmatched-budget and should be replaced by the equal-k delta. Caveat: example count is matched but token length is not reported.

comparison: Table 10 (Section 4.5): Full VulnAgent-R2 vs. w/o graph context optimizer
model_config: Agents use Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, temperature 0.2, in both arms; rest of the multi-agent pipeline (CER, Sceptic, VPS, memory, calibration, scheduler) retained
dataset_metric: PrimeVul (precision/recall/F1), plus ReposVul and JITVul F1
budget_control: Full system has a token-budgeted greedy context selector (at most 16 blocks). Average tokens per sample differ: 9,410 (full) vs 7,810 (w/o optimizer); the arms are not matched
arm_a: Context chosen by the budgeted coverage-utility optimizer over the typed repository graph (callers, callees, data-flow neighbours, validators, tests, configs, historical patches)
arm_b: Context without the graph optimizer (the replacement selection procedure is not described)
other_changes: A pipeline stage (graph-based context optimization) is removed inside a multi-agent tool loop with counterfactual reweighting, dynamic verification, and memory; downstream agent rounds and tool calls vary with it
delta: PrimeVul F1 .385 (full) vs .337 (w/o graph context optimizer), 4.8 pp absolute; ReposVul .624 vs .572; JITVul .606 vs .553
rationale: Table 10 removes an architectural component ('w/o graph context optimizer') from an agentic pipeline, not a representation fed to a fixed model, and the paper does not say what context replaces it. The full arm also uses more tokens (9,410 vs 7,810). The other Table 10 rows (w/o CER, Sceptic, VPS) are verification/agent components and cannot serve as representation ablations.

comparison: Table 2 (Section 4.3): full VulTriage vs. w/o Control Info
model_config: GPT-4o in both arms; temperature 0.7, top-p 1.0 (Table 4); Knowledge Path (top-2 CWE entries) and Semantic Path retained
dataset_metric: PrimeVul pair test subset (131 pairs); P-C, Error, precision, recall, FPR, accuracy, F1
budget_control: not controlled between arms. The Control Path output has an internal 'shared budget that controls the output scale', but removing it shortens the final prompt and no length matching is reported
arm_a: Source code + verbalized AST/CFG/DFG structural context (Level-C granularity) + retrieved CWE knowledge + LLM semantic explanation
arm_b: Source code + retrieved CWE knowledge + LLM semantic explanation (no structural context)
other_changes: none (the Control Path is a deterministic parse-and-verbalize step that only produces prompt content; the other paths are unchanged)
rationale: 'w/o Control Info ... removes the structural context generated from AST, CFG, and DFG' while model and other paths are held fixed, so only supplied context differs. The structured arm is strictly longer and no input-length control between arms is reported.

comparison: Table IV (RQ1, Section V-C): LeanGuard vs. Pure LLM baseline, DeepSeek-V4-Pro backend
model_config: DeepSeek-V4-Pro at temperature 0 for all neural components in both arms; CWE-120/416/476 report best of three runs, CWE-125/415 single runs
dataset_metric: Merged PrimeVul + ReposVul + R2Vul, 5 CWE classes; F1 (also accuracy, precision, recall)
budget_control: not controlled; the pipelines differ in number and type of LLM calls (fact editing, optional refinement) vs a single verdict call
arm_a: Six-stage pipeline: AST candidate extraction, LLM constrained fact-editing filter, deterministic reconciliation and auto-pairing, Lean 4 kernel-checked verification, one-shot neuro-symbolic refinement, evidence-aware adjudication
arm_b: LLM 'reads the function and emits a verdict directly'
other_changes: Symbolic verification stage (Lean 4), deterministic auto-pairing, refinement, and adjudication added. The LLM's task also changes from verdict to fact editor
delta: CWE-416 F1 0.3652 -> 0.5000 (+0.1348 absolute); CWE-415 F1 0.4324 -> 0.6237 (+0.1913 absolute) (Table IV, Pure LLM rows)
rationale: The backend is held fixed ('which isolates the effect of the pipeline from differences in the underlying model'), but the arms differ by a Lean 4 symbolic verifier, auto-pairing and adjudication, and the LLM's role changes from decision maker to 'fact editor'. This is a same-model pipeline ablation, not a representation one. The internal 'w/o AST' ablation (Table V) also changes the LLM's task, so no R-strict comparison exists.
